answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is bonded identity. Every agent must lock a slashable deposit before it can submit answers or grade peers, so spinning up a thousand fake nodes costs a thousand deposits. If an agent submits bogus work or colludes in a grading ring, peers can challenge it and the bond gets cut. Like a wharf that only lets in boats with paid moorings, the entry fee keeps the harbor from filling with ghosts. Reputation then builds slowly, like a glacier, and the trusted nodes form an oasis of reliable peers.
